hero.headline: Oil Prices Jump to $90 a Barrel After U.S. and Iran Exchange Attacks
hero.body:
Crude oil prices surged past $90 a barrel after a two-month window for negotiations between the United States and Iran expired without progress, triggering renewed military exchanges and rattling global energy markets.

Brent crude rose above $90 for the first time since late July, reaching $91.63 by Tuesday morning. The escalation came after Iran signaled it would adopt a more aggressive military stance if talks failed, while President Donald Trump demanded Tehran "put up the white flag of surrender" in a Fox News interview. Trump also threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered with his efforts to resolve the conflict, marking the second time he has directed such a threat at the U.S. strategic partner.

The prospect of expanded conflict alarmed energy analysts watching the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. Roughly a quarter of all seaborne oil normally passes through the waterway. An Iranian military official warned that vessels attempting transit would "find several beautiful holes in their hulls," and a cargo ship was attacked while traveling through the strait early Tuesday.

Ship traffic through the strait plummeted as tensions mounted. Just six cargo vessels transited on Monday, according to ship tracking company Kpler, compared to only five combined on Saturday and Sunday. Angeline Ong, a senior technical analyst at IG, suggested Trump's threat against Oman could mark a turning point for oil markets. "If Muscat pulls back from talks with Tehran, the diplomatic route to restoring normal flows through Hormuz narrows considerably," Ong said, adding that investors might shift from betting on temporary disruption to pricing in prolonged supply problems.

Deutsche Bank analysts interpreted the rising oil prices as evidence that investors were preparing for an extended closure of the strait. The economic consequences rippled across markets. U.S. gasoline prices remained elevated at 37 percent higher than before the conflict began, continuing to pressure household budgets and inflation. Bond yields climbed to multi-year highs as investors reassessed growth and inflation expectations.

Trump indicated he was not rushing to end the conflict, telling Fox News he had "no time schedule" and was "not in a hurry" to reach a deal, despite claiming months earlier that resolution was imminent.

Geopolitical strategists warned of compounding risks. Dan Alamariu at Alpine Macro cautioned that escalation through the fall could produce a "double shock" if combined with Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine. He predicted energy market volatility would spike with sustained, intense Middle East conflict, particularly affecting oil and gas prices.

The developments prompted G20 finance officials to convene in the United States for meetings centered on the economic fallout from the Iran conflict.

cards.headline: Trump announces deal for U.S. access to Venezuelan oil reserves
cards.teaser: President Trump says the U.S. has struck an agreement to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Friday that the U.S. has struck a deal to develop Venezuela's oil reserves, with the American government taking a majority stake in the project. Trump characterized the arrangement as beneficial for Americans, pointing to the nation's vast oil deposits.

Energy experts caution against expecting immediate results. Francisco Monaldi, director of the Latin America Energy Program at Rice University, explained that developing Venezuela's reserves requires substantial time and investment, and would not lead to lower gas prices in the near term.

cards.headline: Russian Drone Campaign Shifts to Daytime Attacks on Kyiv
cards.teaser: Air raids now occur throughout the day in the Ukrainian capital, a change from years of primarily overnight strikes.
cards.body:
Russia has shifted its drone attack strategy in Kyiv to nearly constant air raids throughout the day, departing from years of largely overnight strikes. The change has left residents exhausted and on edge as the war continues.

The new pattern represents a dangerous phase in the conflict, with Ukrainians facing the threat of attack at all hours rather than primarily during nighttime. The relentless pace of the drone campaign has fundamentally altered daily life in the capital.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Faces Rate Decision Pressure After Warsh Speech
cards.teaser: Chair Kevin Warsh sent interest rate hike expectations higher with tough talk on inflation at Jackson Hole.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at Jackson Hole raised market expectations for interest rate hikes, with analysts noting his firm stance on inflation control put the Fed potentially at odds with the Treasury Department. His comments suggested the Fed could pursue rate increases despite broader economic pressures.

The speech prompted market reactions across fixed income securities, with Treasury yields reflecting competing concerns about inflation persistence and economic uncertainty. Analysts highlighted the policy tension between the Fed's inflation-fighting approach and the administration's broader economic priorities.

cards.headline: Trump administration plans to cut U.S. health aid to Africa by more than half
cards.teaser: Planned reductions target programs fighting deadly diseases as the administration pushes developing nations to increase their own spending.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is planning to reduce U.S. health aid to Africa by more than half, according to an analysis of proposed budget changes. The cuts would affect programs that combat the spread of deadly diseases across the continent, representing a substantial decrease in American support for global health initiatives.

The planned reductions align with a broader administration strategy to pressure developing nations to spend more on their own health infrastructure. The timing of the cuts coincides with ongoing administration negotiations to establish new trade and development agreements with African nations, as Trump seeks to reshape U.S. engagement with the continent.

cards.headline: House returns with government funding bill as top priority
cards.teaser: Congress has one week in session before the next recess to pass legislation extending government funding past the midterm elections.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives reconvened Monday for a one-week session with a stopgap spending bill as its primary focus. Lawmakers must pass legislation to extend government funding beyond the midterm elections to prevent a shutdown.

Democratic Rep. Glenn Ivey of Maryland noted that the spending bill will dominate discussions during the brief session. The compressed timeline intensifies the urgency of negotiations as the House works to secure passage before members head back to their districts.

cards.headline: Nepal Resorts to Mass Burials as Flood Death Toll Rises
cards.teaser: Over 4,200 people remain missing, with only a fraction found among the dead so far.
cards.body:
Nepal has begun mass burials as recovery efforts continue following devastating floods near its border with Tibet. Over 4,200 people remain missing, with only a small fraction discovered among the dead, suggesting the death toll will rise significantly in coming days.

Heavy rain has compounded the crisis, trapping relief vehicles and hampering rescue operations. The Nepali army is working to rescue approximately 100 people trapped in a tunnel at a flooded hydropower project. The scale of the disaster has exceeded local capacity for individual burials and body identification.

cards.headline: G20 Finance Officials Meet as Iran War Disrupts Global Economy
cards.teaser: The gathering in the United States focuses on economic impacts from the conflict, including rising oil prices.
cards.body:
Finance officials from G20 nations are meeting in the United States with the Iran war dominating the agenda. The conflict has created an ongoing economic shock, driving up oil prices globally and creating uncertainty across financial markets.

The gathering brings together finance ministers from the world's largest economies to coordinate responses to the war's economic fallout. Oil price increases have rippled through global supply chains, affecting inflation and economic growth projections worldwide.

cards.headline: Nepal's New Prime Minister Faces Flood Recovery Challenge
cards.teaser: Balendra Shah, 36, won office this year on promises to fight corruption and mismanagement.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah, 36, came to power this year amid youth frustration over government corruption and mismanagement. His new administration now confronts a critical challenge as Nepal recovers from devastating floods near its border with Tibet, with thousands still missing.

Heavy rain continues to complicate relief efforts, with muddy roads trapping aid vehicles. The U.S. has pledged $3.5 million in flood assistance, with Catholic Relief Services distributing the first $500,000 to survivors. Shah's coordination of recovery and reconstruction efforts will signal whether his government can fulfill its promises of competent governance.

cards.headline: China's Flood Defenses Overwhelmed by Nepal Disaster
cards.teaser: Officials had strengthened protections at a border crossing after a glacial flood last year, but the recent disaster proved too severe.
cards.body:
Chinese border defenses designed to protect against Himalayan flooding were overwhelmed by last week's disaster in Nepal. Officials had reinforced protections at a border crossing following a glacial flood last year, but the recent cascade of hazards exceeded their capacity.

The flooding presented a different type of disaster than the glacial event China had prepared for. The combination of multiple hazards created conditions that surpassed the strengthened defenses at the crossing. Tibetan advocacy groups claim hundreds of homes were destroyed on the Tibetan side of the border, though Beijing has restricted public discussion of the disaster. Meanwhile, the U.S. pledged $3.5 million in flood aid for Tibet and Nepal, with initial funds distributed through Catholic Relief Services.

cards.headline: Cyprus Ferry Survivors Describe Desperate Escape
cards.teaser: One survivor told Turkish media that her daughter slipped from her hands during the sinking.
cards.body:
A ferry carrying 267 people capsized off the northern Cyprus port city of Kyrenia on Sunday, leaving at least eight people dead and nearly 20 missing. The double-hulled vessel took in water and flipped over just after leaving port, forcing passengers to cling to the upturned hull until rescue arrived.

Survivors were pulled from the water by passing vessels and coastguard members. One survivor recounted the trauma to a Turkish news channel, describing how her daughter slipped from her hands during the chaos. Divers have joined search teams scouring the deep waters as recovery operations continue.

cards.headline: South Korean Church Leader Sentenced for Corruption
cards.teaser: Han Hak-ja received two years in prison for financial dealings related to the former president and first lady.
cards.body:
Han Hak-ja, 83-year-old leader of South Korea's Unification Church, was sentenced to two years in prison for bribery offences. A court found that she gave the former first lady luxury gifts including two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace.

Han, the widow and successor of the church's founder, was convicted in connection with the country's previous leadership. The former president and first lady are also imprisoned as part of broader corruption investigations affecting multiple high-profile figures in South Korean politics and society.

hero.headline: One dead, 15 missing after flash flood tears through Grand Canyon
hero.body:
A major flash flood swept through Arizona's Grand Canyon on Saturday afternoon, killing one person and leaving approximately 15 others missing or unaccounted for, according to the National Park Service.

The flooding occurred in the Bright Angel Canyon area near Phantom Ranch. Park staff and the Arizona Department of Public Safety evacuated more than 60 people by Sunday morning. The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River.

The disaster caused extensive damage to park infrastructure. The flood knocked out the sole water pipeline that supplies up to 6 million annual visitors and about 1,600 residents. This pipeline had been undergoing a $208 million upgrade since 2023. Nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed, and the Colorado River is closed to river traffic due to metal structures and debris in the water.

The National Park Service closed several key areas "until further notice," including Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the Phantom Ranch Canteen and cabins, and the entire North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch. Starting Monday, tourists will not be able to stay overnight at the park's lodges and hotels. Residents have been asked to conserve water.

Park officials have requested public assistance in locating missing people. They are asking anyone with information about hikers or backpackers in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday to contact them. They also want to hear from anyone who held a campground reservation in the affected area.

The intense rainfall created dangerous conditions in the steep terrain. Justin Johndrow, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Flagstaff, explained that approximately half an inch to one inch of rain fell within about 30 minutes in the rocky area with steep elevation changes. "Most of it ran off instantly," Johndrow said. The flooding occurred on the north side of the Grand Canyon where Bright Angel Creek descends about 6,000 feet from the North Rim to the Colorado River.

The large boulders swept into the Colorado River during the flood illustrate the tremendous power of the water. Meteorologists warned that more rain and thunderstorms were possible in the area into Monday.

Flash floods represent a persistent hazard in the Grand Canyon, particularly during monsoon season when intense thunderstorms develop rapidly over the Southwest. The remote locations and steep terrain of the canyon make rescue operations difficult and dangerous for emergency personnel. The incident highlights the risks that hikers and visitors face in the park, especially those in backcountry areas during severe weather events.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes after month of calm
cards.teaser: The U.S. struck Iranian targets for the first time in weeks as fighting reignited over the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
U.S. forces struck targets in the Strait of Hormuz, including Larak Island, in the first American attack since late July. The strike killed two people and injured two others. Iran responded with attacks on U.S. targets in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan, marking the first exchange of fire between the two countries in a month.

The escalation reignited a broader conflict over the strategic shipping lane. President Trump claimed an attack on Kharg, a major Iranian energy hub, though Iran disputed the assertion.

cards.headline: Trump administration announces deal to develop Venezuelan oil reserves
cards.teaser: The U.S. will take a majority stake in developing Venezuela's vast oil reserves under a new agreement.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a significant portion of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves. Venezuelan interim president Delcy Rodríguez defended the agreement on Saturday, insisting her country will maintain ownership and sovereignty over its reserves.

Energy experts have expressed skepticism about the deal, noting it will not lower gas prices for American consumers. The agreement has provoked outrage within Venezuela, contradicting the country's previous stance against handing over control of its oil resources.

cards.headline: Heat deaths far exceed official counts, investigation finds
cards.teaser: A two-year investigation revealed Americans are dying from heat much more often than government records show.
cards.body:
NPR spent two years investigating heat-related deaths across the U.S. and discovered that people are dying from heat exposure far more frequently than official statistics reflect. The investigation reveals a significant gap between actual deaths and what current tracking systems record.

The findings expose critical failures in how heat deaths are documented and reported nationwide. Researchers identified reasons for this undercount and outlined potential solutions, including improved data collection methods and policy changes that could help prevent deaths as temperatures continue to rise.

cards.headline: Many women treated for UTIs did not have infections, study finds
cards.teaser: Women diagnosed with recurrent urinary tract infections often had different conditions causing their symptoms.
cards.body:
A recent study found that many women prescribed antibiotics for recurrent urinary tract infections did not actually have UTIs. Instead, their symptoms stemmed from hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

The misdiagnosis raises concerns about unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions and the growing problem of antibiotic resistance. Identifying the true causes of women's urinary and pelvic symptoms could lead to more effective, targeted treatment approaches.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton laid to rest in Nashville
cards.teaser: A private funeral was held for the singer, who died last week at age 80.
cards.body:
Dolly Parton was laid to rest alongside her husband in Nashville following a private family funeral. The country music icon died on Tuesday at the age of 80.

Parton leaves behind a remarkable legacy spanning decades of musical contributions and philanthropic work. Her Imagination Library, inspired by her father's inability to read, has distributed free books to millions of children worldwide. Tributes have poured in from across music, film and politics, celebrating her enduring impact on popular culture and her generosity to communities globally.

cards.headline: Singapore launches initiative to address birthrate collapse
cards.teaser: The city-state unveiled a national plan focused entirely on reversing declining births.
cards.body:
Singapore has unveiled a national initiative focused entirely on addressing its collapsing birthrate. The government has rolled out a comprehensive plan designed to encourage families to have more children.

Demographers say Singapore's approach includes policy ideas that could benefit American parents facing similar challenges. As birthrates have declined in recent years in the U.S., experts see potential lessons in Singapore's strategy for stabilizing population growth.

cards.headline: G20 Finance Officials Meet as Iran Conflict Affects Global Economy
cards.teaser: Finance ministers and central bankers are convening in the United States with the Iran war expected to dominate discussions.
cards.body:
G20 finance ministers and central bank governors gathered as the Iran conflict continued to roil global markets. Oil prices surged to $90 a barrel following recent attacks, with U.S. gasoline prices remaining 37 percent higher than before the war began.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned the group about risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. In his capacity as chair of the Financial Stability Board, Bailey cautioned that frontier AI models are developing sophisticated autonomy and problem-solving abilities that could destabilize the global financial system, with AI-driven cyber risks emerging as a key concern for regulators.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Faces Rate Decision Pressure After Warsh Speech
cards.teaser: Chair Kevin Warsh sent interest rate hike expectations higher with tough talk on inflation at Jackson Hole.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at Jackson Hole raised market expectations for interest rate hikes, with analysts noting his firm stance on inflation control put the Fed potentially at odds with the Treasury Department. His comments suggested the Fed could pursue rate increases despite broader economic pressures.

The speech prompted market reactions across fixed income securities, with Treasury yields reflecting competing concerns about inflation persistence and economic uncertainty. Analysts highlighted the policy tension between the Fed's inflation-fighting approach and the administration's broader economic priorities.

cards.headline: U.S. Plans New Bank Sanctions to Increase Economic Pressure on Iran
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration will impose new secondary sanctions weekly to isolate Iran financially.
cards.body:
The United States is planning to sanction another bank as part of efforts to maintain economic pressure on Iran during the ongoing conflict. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters the administration expects to impose new secondary sanctions on a weekly basis, targeting financial institutions that facilitate Iranian transactions.

The latest sanctions target branches of Egyptian banks operating in the United Arab Emirates, according to reports. Bessent said the sanctions aim to increase Iran's economic isolation and reduce its ability to access international financial systems.

cards.headline: Pancreatic Cancer Drug Priced at $480,000 Annually Reflects Rising Treatment Costs
cards.teaser: Revolution Medicines set the price for Rasonque, illustrating significant inflation in cancer drug pricing over two decades.
cards.body:
A new pancreatic cancer treatment carries an annual price tag of $480,000, reflecting the steep increase in cancer drug costs over the past twenty years. Revolution Medicines set the price for Rasonque, a medication that joins a growing list of therapies costing hundreds of thousands of dollars per patient per year.

The pricing illustrates trends in the pharmaceutical industry where cancer treatments have seen significant inflation. Drugmakers have steadily raised prices for oncology medications, with new therapies routinely launching at prices that would have been considered extraordinary two decades ago.

cards.headline: U.S. Startup Together AI Partners With Saudi Arabia for Data Center
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company announced a deal to use computing resources from Humain in Saudi Arabia.
cards.body:
Together AI, which serves open-source artificial intelligence models, announced a partnership to use computing capacity from Humain in Saudi Arabia. The deal allows the U.S. startup to access data center resources in the Middle Eastern nation.

The partnership enables Together AI to bypass domestic backlash over data center construction in the United States. The arrangement comes as American communities have raised concerns about the energy demands and local impacts of large-scale data center developments.

cards.headline: Pennsylvania Governor Slows Data Center Approvals Amid Local Backlash
cards.teaser: Gov. Josh Shapiro is reconsidering plans for enormous artificial intelligence data centers despite billions in potential construction investment.
cards.body:
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro is slowing approvals for large artificial intelligence data centers after facing public opposition to the projects. The pullback comes despite the potential for billions of dollars in construction investment in a region affected by the decline of the steel industry.

Some local officials and residents have welcomed the economic development opportunity, viewing the projects as a source of jobs and tax revenue. However, concerns about energy consumption, environmental impact, and infrastructure strain have prompted the governor to reconsider the pace of data center expansion.

hero.headline: 12TB leak reveals decade of unreleased Valve games and cut content
hero.teaser: A massive data leak from Steam has exposed files from unreleased games, including early builds of Half-Life 2: Episode 3 and cut Portal 2 content.
hero.body:
A 12-terabyte archive from Valve has leaked online, revealing more than a decade of gaming history that was never publicly released. The files include builds of Half-Life 2: Episode 3, a long-awaited sequel that was never completed, along with cut content from Portal 2 and other Valve projects.

Fans have begun examining the leaked materials, uncovering early assets and development files from various Valve games. The archive provides a look at abandoned projects and content that was removed before final releases. The leak represents one of the largest collections of unreleased gaming material to surface publicly.

cards.headline: NASA launches Roman Space Telescope to map universe and study dark energy
cards.teaser: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on Sunday, beginning a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and investigate dark energy an.
cards.body:
NASA successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will embark on a three-month journey to the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2) beyond the Moon. From this distant vantage point, the telescope will conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe to study dark matter and dark energy.

Named after NASA's first chief astronomer, the Roman telescope features a field of view 100 times larger than Hubble's infrared instrument, enabling it to capture wide panoramas of space and survey large portions of the sky more efficiently. The mission represents a significant milestone in space exploration and continues NASA's tradition of deploying powerful space-based observatories to answer fundamental questions about the cosmos.

cards.headline: GTA VI gameplay preview draws over 4 million live viewers
cards.teaser: An extended gameplay preview of Grand Theft Auto VI attracted more than 4 million simultaneous viewers, signaling high demand for the upcoming release.
cards.body:
Rockstar Games' first official gameplay reveal of Grand Theft Auto VI attracted millions of viewers across streaming platforms. The broadcast showcased the game's third-person gunplay mechanics and cinematic presentation, featuring sequences with slow-motion kill shots reminiscent of titles like Fallout 3. The footage depicted familiar GTA territory including crime scenarios and action-oriented gameplay.

The preview generated significant media coverage, with gaming outlets providing live coverage of the reveal. GTA VI is positioned as one of the year's most anticipated releases, with industry observers expecting it to become a major commercial success when it launches.

cards.headline: Northern lights may appear in nine states following geomagnetic storm
cards.teaser: A geomagnetic storm could make the northern lights visible across nine US states, including areas farther south than usual.
cards.body:
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration issued geomagnetic storm watches predicting auroras could be visible from states including Michigan and Connecticut. The storms result from solar activity that sends charged particles toward Earth, creating light displays when they interact with the atmosphere.

Visibility depends on weather conditions and the strength of the geomagnetic activity. The NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center tracks these events and issues watches when conditions favor aurora sightings at lower latitudes than normal. Clear skies increase the chances of seeing the phenomenon.

cards.headline: Apple sets September 9 date for iPhone 18 launch event
cards.teaser: Apple will hold its annual iPhone launch event on September 9, the first major product unveiling under new CEO Ternus.
cards.body:
Apple announced a September 9 event for the launch of the iPhone 18, marking the first major product release under new CEO John Ternus. The event, themed "Surprise and Shine," is expected to include announcements for the iPhone 18 Pro, new iPad mini models, and potential home products.

Reports suggest pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro may start later than in previous years. Speculation continues about whether Apple will announce a folding iPhone model, though no official confirmation has been provided. The event follows Apple's traditional September timeline for major product launches.

cards.headline: US builds barriers around drones and robots as China competition shifts
cards.teaser: The United States is implementing new restrictions on foreign-made drones and robots, but China's manufacturing scale may allow competition to continue elsewhere.
cards.body:
The US is implementing new restrictions on foreign-made drones and autonomous robots, particularly targeting Chinese manufacturers, as part of broader national security efforts and domestic manufacturing promotion.

However, China's substantial manufacturing scale may allow it to circumvent these barriers by redirecting products to less-restricted markets globally. This shift could limit how effectively US restrictions reshape the international robotics and drone competition landscape.

cards.headline: Grindr CEO defends strategy to expand beyond dating into health and AI
cards.teaser: Grindr CEO George Arison outlined plans to transform the app into a comprehensive platform for gay men, including healthcare services and AI features.
cards.body:
George Arison, CEO of Grindr, detailed his vision to expand the dating app into what he calls a "gayborhood in your pocket," incorporating artificial intelligence, healthcare services, and long-distance matchmaking. The company introduced a premium tier priced above $350 that has generated investor scrutiny.

Arison said he is addressing what he describes as Wall Street's undervaluation of the company. He has been promoting the expansion strategy since 2022, aiming to make Grindr more than a dating platform. The approach represents a shift from the app's core hookup and dating functions toward broader lifestyle services.

hero.headline: Djokovic exits US Open in first round
hero.body:
Novak Djokovic's US Open campaign ended in distress during a first-round match that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. The 39-year-old Serbian star was defeated 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 by Argentina's Mariano Navone around midnight, leaving the court in tears.

This marks only the third first-round exit of Djokovic's career and his earliest departure from a Grand Slam since the 2006 Australian Open, when he was 18 years old. The loss came at his record-extending 84th Grand Slam appearance.

The match revealed serious physical struggles for Djokovic. Barely 15 minutes into play, he was already visibly struggling with the conditions. Throughout the five sets, he repeatedly vomited into the towel bin, experienced severe cramping, fought for balance, and appeared disoriented on court. Between panting desperately from the baseline and battling physical deterioration, he looked increasingly helpless as the match progressed.

Djokovic attributed his difficulties to a health condition exacerbated by heat and humidity. He described the experience bluntly after the match: "It is something that I've been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year. You know, vomiting, throwing up, serious issue there, and then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain, and the back just gave up in the end."

This was not an isolated incident. Two weeks earlier at the Cincinnati Open, Djokovic struggled similarly against another Argentine player in comparable evening humidity conditions, losing in three sets to Thiago Agustín Tirante, who appeared unaffected by the weather.

On paper, this should have been a favorable draw. Navone, a 25-year-old ranked just inside the top 50, had built most of his success on clay courts. However, the Argentine player proved equal to the challenge. As a longtime admirer of Djokovic, Navone had posted supportive tweets about the Serbian star as a teenager and approached the match with focused intensity. His parents even abandoned a Caribbean holiday to attend after learning of the draw.

Navone played a solid match, maintaining consistent depth from both wings and forcing extended exchanges that Djokovic's deteriorating body could not handle. The younger player chased down every ball and kept the pressure consistently applied.

Despite his physical distress, Djokovic's serving kept him competitive for much of the evening. His exceptional serve allowed him to secure a two-sets-to-one lead through the fourth set, but by that point his legs felt heavy and his first serve began to falter. He could not recover, ultimately walking off court with nothing left to offer.

The defeat underscores the mounting challenges Djokovic faces at 39, competing at tennis's highest level against younger, physically fresher opponents.

cards.headline: Venus Williams loses 15th straight match at US Open
cards.teaser: Venus Williams extended her losing streak to 15 consecutive singles matches with a first-round loss at the US Open.
cards.body:
Venus Williams' record-extending 26th US Open appearance ended in a first-round loss to Sofia Kenin, 6-2, 7-6 (6). At age 46 and ranked 611th, Williams took the court after midnight—the match finally began at 12:13am, the latest start in US Open history, following Novak Djokovic's five-set defeat.

The loss extends Williams' winless streak to 15 consecutive tour-level matches. Despite not winning a singles match in over a year, the seven-time Grand Slam champion continues to receive wildcards to compete, with reasons for her participation extending beyond competitive results.

cards.headline: Manchester City sign Germany defender Wamser
cards.teaser: Manchester City completed the signing of Bayer Leverkusen defender Carlotta Wamser on a four-year contract.
cards.body: The defender joins Manchester City's squad as they strengthen their defensive options ahead of the new season.

cards.headline: British tight end Traore makes Dolphins opening roster
cards.teaser: Seydou Traore became the first British tight end to make an NFL opening day roster with the Miami Dolphins.
cards.body:
British tight end Seydou Traore has been included in the Miami Dolphins' initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. This means he will be eligible to play from the start of the regular season.

Traore's inclusion on the Dolphins' roster marks a notable achievement for British players in professional American football.

cards.headline: NFL teams finalize 53-man rosters across league
cards.teaser: All 32 NFL teams completed their roster cuts to reach the league-mandated 53-player limit for the regular season.
cards.body:
NFL teams across the league finalized their 53-man rosters following the deadline for cuts. Teams made final decisions about which players would make their opening day rosters and which would be released or placed on injured reserve. The Patriots placed a rising offensive lineman on injured reserve while cutting a veteran defensive lineman.

Former Syracuse quarterback Kyle McCord was among the players who survived cuts and made an NFL roster. The roster decisions represent months of evaluation during training camp and preseason games. Teams now have their rosters set for the start of the 2026 regular season, though they can still make adjustments through waivers and free agency as the season progresses.

cards.headline: Actress turned tennis player Frodin enters US Open
cards.teaser: Thea Frodin, who played a young Serena Williams on screen, is competing in her first US Open.
cards.body:
Teenager Thea Frodin is set to compete at the US Open after previously portraying a young Serena Williams in a film. The young player is following in the footsteps of the American tennis legend she once depicted on the big screen. Frodin's transition from acting to professional tennis represents an unusual path to the sport's biggest stages.

Frodin's entry into the US Open marks a significant milestone in her tennis career. The teenager is among the younger competitors in the draw at Flushing Meadows. Her background in acting and her connection to Williams' story add a unique narrative to her tennis journey as she competes in one of the sport's four major championships.

cards.headline: Emery addresses Chelsea and Aston Villa transfers
cards.teaser: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery said the relationship between his club and Chelsea is business-focused after multiple player moves.
cards.body:
Unai Emery has emphasized that Aston Villa and Chelsea are rivals rather than partners, despite their frequent player transfers. The Villa manager stated the clubs want to "kill" each other on the pitch, characterizing their dealings as purely transactional rather than based on friendly relations.

This summer has seen significant movement between the two Premier League sides. Chelsea paid £117m for Morgan Rogers, while Villa acquired Nicolas Jackson for a deal worth up to £65m and Alejandro Garnacho on loan with a conditional obligation to buy. Emiliano Martínez also recently moved between the clubs, exemplifying the ongoing business between them.

hero.headline: Dolly Parton buried in Nashville following private family funeral
hero.body:
Country music legend Dolly Parton was laid to rest in Nashville alongside her husband following a private family funeral. The singer died on Tuesday at the age of 80 after suffering from cancer.

Parton's death marks the loss of one of the most celebrated and influential figures in American music history. Over a career spanning more than six decades, she became known for her distinctive voice and songwriting, but also for her humanitarian work and business ventures.

The private ceremony reflects the family's desire for an intimate farewell to the entertainer who had touched millions of lives. Parton had been married to Carl Dean, who remained largely out of the public eye throughout their decades-long marriage.

Parton possessed a distinctive soprano with a remarkable vibrato and east Tennessee twang that made her voice among the most recognizable in music. Her wit was equally famous, with self-deprecating humor that endeared her to audiences worldwide. Her maxim "It takes a lot of money to look this cheap" captured her appetite for glitz and mischief that defined her public persona.

She was a pioneering figure in taking country music into the mainstream, becoming one of the first country stars to achieve significant crossover success. At the 2014 Glastonbury festival, she attracted what was reportedly the largest crowd in the event's history, performing while wearing a crystal-studded white suit and tooting a rhinestone saxophone.

Her songwriting prowess earned her recognition across the industry, with 10 Grammy awards, 11 from the Academy of Country Music, and numerous other honors. Her composition "I Will Always Love You" became one of the best-selling singles of all time after Whitney Houston recorded it for "The Bodyguard" soundtrack in 1992. The song earned Parton enough money, she said, "to buy Graceland" and proved that her refusal to share publishing rights with Elvis Presley when he wanted to record it had been the right decision.

Beyond music, Parton's charitable work reflected her commitment to helping others. From 1988, she provided support to local schoolchildren, and from 1995, she ran an international book reading programme. She also provided aid for people affected by wildfires and hurricanes and supported medical research. Her Imagination Library became known worldwide for distributing free books to millions of children, inspired in part by her father's inability to read.

Though known for her glamorous exterior and larger-than-life persona, Parton grounded her public image with deep intelligence and honesty. She remained active in her career and charitable work until recent years, leaving behind a lasting impact on generations of musicians who followed in her footsteps and a legacy that extended far beyond music into film, television, and popular culture.

cards.headline: Anne Hathaway joins Tom Cruise in Days of Thunder sequel
cards.teaser: Paramount sets release date for follow-up to 1990 racing film as original cast member criticizes casting choice.
cards.body:
Anne Hathaway has signed on to star alongside Tom Cruise in a sequel to the 1990 racing film Days of Thunder, with Paramount setting a release date for the project. The follow-up marks a return to the franchise more than three decades after the original film.

Randy Quaid, who appeared in the first film, publicly criticized the casting decision, calling Hathaway a horrible choice for the sequel. The original Days of Thunder starred Cruise as a stock car racer and featured Nicole Kidman in a prominent role.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo hosts Daisy Chain Fields festival featuring superstars and nonprofits
cards.teaser: The singer brought together performers including Stevie Nicks and Sarah McLachlan for an event promoting organizations that support women and girls.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo's inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival in June brought together an impressive lineup of female and female-fronted artists. The festival featured performances from Chappell Roan, Mitski, the Breeders, Bikini Kill, Garbage, Karen O, Sarah McLachlan, and Stevie Nicks, among others.

The event combined live music with support for nonprofits focused on women's and girls' well-being, creating a celebration of female artistry and charitable causes. Rodrigo curated the festival to showcase established artists she admires while highlighting organizations dedicated to issues affecting women and girls.

cards.headline: Naomi Watts to receive award at San Sebastián Film Festival
cards.teaser: The British actor will be honored with the Donostia Award at the festival's 74th edition in September.
cards.body:
Naomi Watts will receive the prestigious Donostia Award at the San Sebastián Film Festival during its 74th edition in September. She joins German director Werner Herzog, whose Donostia Award was announced in early August.

Watts will accept the award on Saturday, September 19, with the festival screening The Housewife, the directorial debut of Canadian filmmaker Ben Shirinian. The Donostia Award represents one of the festival's highest honors for contributions to cinema.

cards.headline: Roger Waters joins Palestinian art documentary as executive producer
cards.teaser: The Pink Floyd co-founder has signed on to support a debut feature film about a resistance fighter turned artist in the Jenin refugee camp.
cards.body:
Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has joined filmmaker Rishi Pelham's debut feature documentary Freedom Theatre as executive producer. The film follows Ahmed Tobasi, a resistance fighter who became an artist working in the Jenin refugee camp in Palestine.

Described as an immersive and sensory character study, the documentary explores Tobasi's efforts to maintain creative work within the refugee camp. Waters' involvement as executive producer brings significant profile to the independent documentary project.

cards.headline: NBCUniversal and U-Next announce partnership in Japan
cards.teaser: The agreement brings Universal+ streaming exclusively to Japan's second-largest video platform and includes theme park and content distribution initiatives.
cards.body:
NBCUniversal and U-Next have formed a long-term strategic partnership in Japan that brings NBCUniversal's international streaming brand Universal+ exclusively to the U-Next platform. The deal also includes joint initiatives with Universal Studios Japan and new distribution pathways for Japanese content globally.

U-Next, operated by Usen U-Next Group, ranks as Japan's second-largest subscription video-on-demand platform behind Netflix, with more than several million subscribers. The partnership represents a significant expansion of NBCUniversal's presence in the Japanese market across both streaming and theme park operations.

cards.headline: DraftKings launches advertising campaign featuring Kevin Hart and Nick Jonas
cards.teaser: The sports-wagering company debuts what it expects to be a long-running series of commercials centered on a road trip concept.
cards.body:
DraftKings has launched a new advertising campaign featuring comedian Kevin Hart and musician Nick Jonas in what the company anticipates will be a significant and long-running effort. The commercial depicts Hart and Jonas on an extended road trip promoting the platform's wagering and predictions features.

Jonas plays a prominent role in the campaign, which marks a major marketing push for the sports-wagering giant. The road trip concept provides the framework for showcasing DraftKings' various betting products and services.

hero.headline: Trump announces deal for U.S. access to Venezuelan oil reserves
hero.teaser: President Trump says the U.S. has struck an agreement to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil.
hero.body:
President Trump announced Friday that the U.S. has struck a deal to develop Venezuela's oil reserves, with the American government taking a majority stake in the project. Trump characterized the arrangement as beneficial for Americans, pointing to the nation's vast oil deposits.

Energy experts caution against expecting immediate results. Francisco Monaldi, director of the Latin America Energy Program at Rice University, explained that developing Venezuela's reserves requires substantial time and investment, and would not lead to lower gas prices in the near term.

cards.headline: Trump administration plans to cut U.S. health aid to Africa by more than half
cards.teaser: Planned reductions target programs fighting deadly diseases as the administration pushes developing nations to increase their own spending.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is planning to reduce U.S. health aid to Africa by more than half, according to an analysis of proposed budget changes. The cuts would affect programs that combat the spread of deadly diseases across the continent, representing a substantial decrease in American support for global health initiatives.

The planned reductions align with a broader administration strategy to pressure developing nations to spend more on their own health infrastructure. The timing of the cuts coincides with ongoing administration negotiations to establish new trade and development agreements with African nations, as Trump seeks to reshape U.S. engagement with the continent.

cards.headline: House returns with government funding bill as top priority
cards.teaser: Congress has one week in session before the next recess to pass legislation extending government funding past the midterm elections.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives reconvened Monday for a one-week session with a stopgap spending bill as its primary focus. Lawmakers must pass legislation to extend government funding beyond the midterm elections to prevent a shutdown.

Democratic Rep. Glenn Ivey of Maryland noted that the spending bill will dominate discussions during the brief session. The compressed timeline intensifies the urgency of negotiations as the House works to secure passage before members head back to their districts.

cards.headline: Republicans begin planning for post-Trump era ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: GOP strategists say the party needs to define its direction before Trump becomes a lame duck after the 2026 midterms.
cards.body:
Republican strategists and political experts say the party faces a period of internal debate about its future direction as President Trump approaches the final years of his term. The discussion has gained urgency with the approaching midterm election and the recognition that Trump will become a lame duck after voters go to the polls in November.

Republicans acknowledge the party will need substantial reflection to chart its course once Trump leaves office in 2029. The conversation about the GOP's post-Trump identity is starting earlier than in previous administrations, as party leaders and strategists attempt to position themselves for the transition while Trump still holds office.

cards.headline: Trump makes himself central figure in midterm campaigns
cards.teaser: Vulnerable Republican candidates cannot afford to distance themselves from the president, who controls a $400 million war chest.
cards.body:
President Trump and Democrats both want the upcoming midterm elections to focus on Trump himself, creating a dynamic where vulnerable Republican candidates must carefully manage their relationship with the president. Republicans facing competitive races cannot risk antagonizing Trump because they need his support to energize his base of voters.

Trump controls a $400 million campaign war chest that Republican candidates depend on for their races. This financial leverage gives the president substantial influence over how Republicans campaign and position themselves in the midterms, limiting their ability to create distance even in districts where Trump may be unpopular.

cards.headline: Democrats compete for House Energy and Commerce Committee seats
cards.teaser: Members anticipating a potential majority are positioning themselves for openings on the influential panel.
cards.body:
House Democrats who believe they have a chance of retaking the majority in the midterm elections are making moves to secure seats on the House Energy and Commerce Committee. The committee is considered one of the most powerful panels in Congress due to its jurisdiction over health care, telecommunications, and energy policy.

A number of seats on the committee are expected to open up, and Democrats are beginning their campaigns for those positions months before the election. The early jockeying reflects confidence among some Democrats about their prospects in November and the high value members place on serving on the influential committee.

cards.headline: Michigan Senate race tests impact of political associations for Democrats
cards.teaser: The Senate contest in a critical state puts focus on how candidates' connections influence voter decisions.
cards.body:
Democrats face a test of how political associations affect electoral prospects in Michigan's Senate race, which party strategists consider critical to maintaining their majority. The race has drawn attention to questions about which relationships and endorsements help or hurt candidates in competitive contests.

Michigan represents a key battleground in the fight for Senate control. The outcome could determine whether Democrats retain their majority or Republicans gain the upper hand in the chamber. How voters weigh candidates' political connections and affiliations may provide insights applicable to other close races across the country.
